mmio.interrupts: 30 raw sticky events, independent enable/masked status, W1C through INT_RAW or INT_CLR; enabled pending IRQ level is retained across clock gates and dependency pauses; one IRQ per group

clocks.pll-f160m-clk: PWM/group/timer/deadtime/carrier source; actual connected frequency only
clocks.apb-clk: 32-bit capture timer source; actual connected frequency only
clocks.clock-enable: named level GPIO, freezes counters and pending delays; physical source retains output level and OE while gated
clocks.reset-held: named level GPIO, clears generator state on assertion and blocks MMIO while held; reset output state is driven through actual GPIO matrix/pad OE
clocks.reset: named rising/high strobe GPIO, unconditional peripheral reset
clocks.soc_reset_policy: CPU-only reset preserves controller; chip/peripheral reset clears it

deadtime cascade and carrier carry rounded-ns overshoot

reference_interpretations.rule: UTEZ and DTEP; symmetric cycle uses pinned LL peak convention
reference_interpretations.conflict: TRM introductory prose says 2*period+1, while pinned LL and TRM endpoint range note describe [0,period-1]+[period,1]; implementation follows the latter.
TRM formula omits the +1 encoded by pinned LL; implementation follows LL used by IDF.

reference_interpretations.rule: zero action contributes no set/clear/toggle request; highest-priority nonzero request wins independently for each output
reference_interpretations.evidence: [INFERENCE] TRM event priority tables plus ordinary IDF single-comparator configuration, where the unused comparator remains zero and must not suppress TEZ.

reference_interpretations.rule: Software-force event immediately sets generator output; next active timing event may alter that actual forced output, including toggle. No separate transient output override.
references: TRM v1.8 p1348 Software-Force Events and Figure36.3-19

reference_interpretations.topic: one-shot brake clear and handler activation
reference_interpretations.rule: FH_CLR_OST rising edge clears ongoing OST; unchanged active fault level does not re-arm it. A new physical fault activation or newly enabling its OST handler can trigger a new OST.
reference_interpretations.inference: Enabling handler on an already-active fault is treated as a new gated fault activation; no physical metrology claim.

provider_boundaries: GPIO matrix owns pad routing, inversion, IE and GPIO synchronization; MCPWM does not synthesize a second pad signal store.
Analog thresholds, power, net contention and settling belong to the electrical owner.
QEMU virtual nanoseconds expose sub-ns source phase through retained integer remainders, not measured silicon timing.
